sanskrit: tataḥ sītām upāgamya rākṣasyo vikṛtānanāḥ paruṣaṃ paruṣā nārya ūcus tā vākyam apriyam
english: Then the rākṣasīs, hideous of face, approached Sītā, and those harsh women spoke harsh and unpleasant words to her.

sanskrit: kiṃ tvam antaḥpure sīte sarvabhūtamanohare mahārhaśayanopete na vāsam anumanyase
english: "Sītā, why do you not consent to live in this inner palace — delightful to all beings and furnished with the most worthy couches?"

sanskrit: mānuṣī mānuṣasyaiva bhāryātvaṃ bahu manyase pratyāhara mano rāmān na tvaṃ jātu bhaviṣyasi
english: "You are a mortal woman, and you prize so highly being the wife of a mere mortal. Turn your mind away from Rāma — you will never be his again."

sanskrit: mānuṣī mānuṣaṃ taṃ tu rāmam icchasi śobhane rājyād bhraṣṭam asiddhārthaṃ viklavaṃ tam anindite
english: "You are a mortal woman, yet you desire that mortal Rāma — he who has been cast out of his kingdom, whose purpose has not been accomplished, and who is miserable and forlorn, O blameless one."

sanskrit: rākṣasīnāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā sītā padmanibhekṣaṇā netrābhyām aśrupūrṇābhyām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having heard the words of the rākṣasīs, Sītā, lotus-eyed, with both eyes brimming with tears, spoke these words.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ lokavidviṣṭam udāharatha saṃgatāḥ naitan manasi vākyaṃ me kilbiṣaṃ pratitiṣṭhati
english: "What you all say together is hateful to the world; that sinful speech does not take root in my mind."

sanskrit: na mānuṣī rākṣasasya bhāryā bhavitum arhati kāmaṃ khādata māṃ sarvā na kariṣyāmi vo vacaḥ dīno vā rājyahīno vā yo me bhartā sa me guruḥ
english: "A mortal woman does not deserve to be the wife of a rākṣasa. Eat me if you will, all of you — I will not do your bidding. Whether destitute or stripped of his kingdom, whoever is my husband is my lord."

sanskrit: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasyaḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ bhartsayanti sma paruṣair vākyai rāvaṇacoditāḥ
english: Having heard Sītā's words, the rākṣasīs, overwhelmed with rage and urged on by Rāvaṇa, began to threaten her with harsh words.

sanskrit: avalīnaḥ sa nirvākyo hanumāñ śiṃśapādrume sītāṃ saṃtarjayantīs tā rākṣasīr aśṛṇot kapiḥ
english: Hanumān, hidden and silent in the śiṃśapā tree, heard those rākṣasīs as they fiercely threatened Sītā.

sanskrit: tām abhikramya saṃrabdhā vepamānāṃ samantataḥ bhṛśaṃ saṃlilihur dīptān pralambadaśanacchadān
english: Rushing at her furiously from all sides as she trembled, they licked their blazing, protruding lips again and again.

sanskrit: ūcuś ca paramakruddhāḥ pragṛhyāśu paraśvadhān neyam arhati bhartāraṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam
english: And utterly enraged, quickly brandishing their battle-axes, they said: "She does not deserve Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, as her husband."

sanskrit: sā bhartsyamānā bhīmābhī rākṣasībhir varānanā sā bāṣpam apamārjantī śiṃśapāṃ tām upāgamat
english: She — the lovely-faced one — being menaced by those terrible rākṣasīs, wiping away her tears, drew near to that śiṃśapā tree.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ śiṃśapāṃ sītā rākṣasībhiḥ samāvṛtā abhigamya viśālākṣī tasthau śokapariplutā
english: Then Sītā, wide-eyed, surrounded by the rākṣasīs, approached that śiṃśapā and stood there, utterly submerged in grief.

sanskrit: tāṃ kṛśāṃ dīnavadanāṃ malināmbaradhāriṇīm bhartsayāṃ cakrire bhīmā rākṣasyas tāḥ samantataḥ
english: Those terrible rākṣasīs fell to threatening her on all sides — her who was thin, wearing a dejected face, and clad in soiled garments.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ vinatā nāma rākṣasī bhīmadarśanā abravīt kupitākārā karālā nirṇatodarī
english: Then a rākṣasī named Vinatā, fearsome to behold, gaunt-bellied and fierce, with the bearing of one enraged, addressed her.

sanskrit: sīte paryāptam etāvad bhartṛsneho nidarśitaḥ sarvatrātikṛtaṃ bhadre vyasanāyopakalpate
english: "Sītā, enough — you have shown your love for your husband sufficiently. O auspicious one, excess in all things leads to ruin."

sanskrit: parituṣṭāsmi bhadraṃ te mānuṣas te kṛto vidhiḥ mamāpi tu vacaḥ pathyaṃ bruvantyāḥ kuru maithili
english: "I am satisfied; well done, the rites due to your mortal husband have been observed. But heed also my words, O Maithilī, who speak for your benefit."

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ bhaja bhartāraṃ bhartāraṃ sarvarakṣasām vikrāntaṃ rūpavantaṃ ca sureśam iva vāsavam
english: "Embrace Rāvaṇa as your husband — the lord of all rākṣasas, valiant and handsome, like Vāsava the king of gods."

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaṃ tyāgaśīlaṃ ca sarvasya priyavādinam mānuṣaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ rāmaṃ tyaktvā rāvaṇam āśraya
english: "Forsake the wretched mortal Rāma — noble, generous, and dear-speaking though he be to all — and seek refuge in Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: divyāṅgarāgā vaidehi divyābharaṇabhūṣitā adya prabhṛti sarveṣāṃ lokānām īśvarī bhava agneḥ svāhā yathā devī śacīvendrasya śobhane
english: "O Vaidehī, anointed with divine perfumes, adorned with divine ornaments, become from this day the mistress of all the worlds — as Svāhā is to Agni, as Śacī to Indra, O beautiful one."

sanskrit: kiṃ te rāmeṇa vaidehi kṛpaṇena gatāyuṣā
english: "What is Rāma to you, O Vaidehī — that wretched man whose lifespan is spent?"

sanskrit: etad uktaṃ ca me vākyaṃ yadi tvaṃ na kariṣyasi asmin muhūrte sarvās tvāṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmahe vayam
english: "And if you do not act on the words I have spoken, we will devour you this very instant, all of us together."

sanskrit: anyā tu vikaṭā nāma lambamānapayodharā abravīt kupitā sītāṃ muṣṭim udyamya garjatī
english: Then another, named Vikaṭā, with dangling pendulous breasts, angered and roaring, raised her fist and addressed Sītā.

sanskrit: bahūny apratirūpāṇi vacanāni sudurmate anukrośān mṛdutvāc ca soḍhāni tava maithili na ca naḥ kuruṣe vākyaṃ hitaṃ kālapuraskṛtam
english: "Many unseemly words from you, O foolish one, have been endured by us out of compassion and gentleness, O Maithilī — yet you still do not act on our timely, beneficial counsel."

sanskrit: ānītāsi samudrasya pāram anyair durāsadam rāvaṇāntaḥpuraṃ ghoraṃ praviṣṭā cāsi maithili
english: "You have been brought by others across the ocean, which is difficult to traverse; you have entered the terrible inner palace of Rāvaṇa, O Maithilī."

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya gṛhe rudhā asmābhis tu surakṣitā na tvāṃ śaktaḥ paritrātum api sākṣāt puraṃdaraḥ
english: "Confined in Rāvaṇa's house and well-guarded by us, not even Purandara himself in person is capable of rescuing you."

sanskrit: kuruṣva hitavādinyā vacanaṃ mama maithili alam aśruprapātena tyaja śokam anarthakam
english: "Do as I say, O Maithilī, for I speak what is beneficial. Enough of these flowing tears — abandon this purposeless grief."

sanskrit: bhaja prītiṃ praharṣaṃ ca tyajaitāṃ nityadainyatām sīte rākṣasarājena saha krīḍa yathāsukham
english: "Embrace joy and delight; give up this perpetual wretchedness. Sītā, sport with the king of the rākṣasas as you please."

sanskrit: jānāsi hi yathā bhīru strīṇāṃ yauvanam adhruvam yāvan na te vyatikrāmet tāvat sukham avāpnuhi
english: "For you know, O timid one, how fleeting is the youth of women. Before it slips away from you, enjoy pleasure."

sanskrit: udyānāni ca ramyāṇi parvatopavanāni ca saha rākṣasarājena cara tvaṃ madirekṣaṇe
english: "Roam the lovely gardens and mountain-groves together with the king of the rākṣasas, O you of intoxicating eyes."

sanskrit: strīsahasrāṇi te sapta vaśe sthāsyanti sundari rāvaṇaṃ bhaja bhartāraṃ bhartāraṃ sarvarakṣasām
english: "Seven thousands of women will remain at your command, O beautiful one. Embrace Rāvaṇa as your husband, the lord of all rākṣasas."

sanskrit: utpāṭya vā te hṛdayaṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmi maithili yadi me vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ na yathāvat kariṣyasi
english: "Or I shall tear out your heart and devour it, O Maithilī, if you do not act on the words I have spoken as I have told you."

sanskrit: tataś caṇḍodarī nāma rākṣasī krūradarśanā bhrāmayantī mahac chūlam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then a rākṣasī named Caṇḍodarī, cruel in appearance, whirling a great spear, spoke these words.

sanskrit: imāṃ hariṇalokākṣīṃ trāsotkampapayodharām rāvaṇena hṛtāṃ dṛṣṭvā daurhṛdo me mahān abhūt
english: "Upon seeing this woman with eyes like those of a doe, her breasts trembling in terror, abducted by Rāvaṇa, a great craving seized me."

sanskrit: yakṛtplīham athotpīḍaṃ hṛdayaṃ ca sabandhanam antrāṇy api tathā śīrṣaṃ khādeyam iti me matiḥ
english: "My mind is set on devouring her liver, her spleen, her heart with its vessels, her entrails, and her head too."

sanskrit: tatas tu praghasā nāma rākṣasī vākyam abravīt kaṇṭham asyā nṛśaṃsāyāḥ pīḍayāmaḥ kim āsyate
english: Then a rākṣasī named Praghasā spoke: "Why do we wait? Let us squeeze the throat of this cruel woman."

sanskrit: nivedyatāṃ tato rājñe mānuṣī sā mṛteti ha nātra kaś cana saṃdehaḥ khādateti sa vakṣyati
english: "Then let it be reported to the king that the mortal woman is dead. There is no doubt he will say: 'Eat her then.'"

sanskrit: tatas tv ajāmukhī nāma rākṣasī vākyam abravīt viśasyemāṃ tataḥ sarvān samān kuruta pīlukān
english: Then a rākṣasī named Ajāmukhī spoke: "Slaughter her, then make even morsels of everything."

sanskrit: vibhajāma tataḥ sarvā vivādo me na rocate peyam ānīyatāṃ kṣipraṃ mālyaṃ ca vividhaṃ bahu
english: "Then let us all divide the portions — I have no liking for quarreling. Let drink be fetched quickly, and garlands of many kinds in abundance."

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā nāma rākṣasī vākyam abravīt ajāmukhā yad uktaṃ hi tad eva mama rocate
english: Then a rākṣasī named Śūrpaṇakhā spoke: "What Ajāmukhā has said is exactly what pleases me too."

sanskrit: surā cānīyatāṃ kṣipraṃ sarvaśokavināśinī mānuṣaṃ māṃsam āsādya nṛtyāmo 'tha nikumbhilām
english: "And let wine be quickly brought — the destroyer of all sorrow. Having obtained this human flesh, let us dance at the Nikumbhilā shrine."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃbhartsyamānā sā sītā surasutopamā rākṣasībhiḥ sughorābhir dhairyam utsṛjya roditi
english: Thus threatened in this manner by those utterly terrible rākṣasīs, Sītā — who resembled the daughter of a god — abandoned her composure and wept.

sanskrit: tathā tāsāṃ vadantīnāṃ paruṣaṃ dāruṇaṃ bahu rākṣasīnām asaumyānāṃ ruroda janakātmajā
english: As those unsightly rākṣasīs spoke many harsh and dreadful words in this way, the daughter of Janaka wept.

sanskrit: evam uktā tu vaidehī rākṣasībhir manasvinī uvāca paramatrastā bāṣpagadgadayā girā
english: But Vaidehī, that high-minded woman, thus addressed by the rākṣasīs, spoke in a voice choked with tears, utterly trembling with fear.

sanskrit: na mānuṣī rākṣasasya bhāryā bhavitum arhati kāmaṃ khādata māṃ sarvā na kariṣyāmi vo vacaḥ
english: "A mortal woman does not deserve to become the wife of a rākṣasa. Eat me, all of you, if you will — I will not do your bidding."

sanskrit: sā rākṣasī madhyagatā sītā surasutopamā na śarma lebhe duḥkhārtā rāvaṇena ca tarjitā
english: She, Sītā — who resembled the daughter of a god — standing in the midst of the rākṣasīs, found no peace, afflicted by grief and threatened by Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: vepate smādhikaṃ sītā viśantīvāṅgam ātmanaḥ vane yūthaparibhraṣṭā mṛgī kokair ivārditā
english: Sītā shuddered violently, as though her own limbs were failing her — like a doe separated from her herd in the forest and harassed by cuckoos.

sanskrit: sā tv aśokasya vipulāṃ śākhām ālambya puṣpitām cintayām āsa śokena bhartāraṃ bhagnamānasā
english: She, supporting herself on a large flowering branch of the aśoka tree, thought with grief of her husband, her heart broken.

sanskrit: sā snāpayantī vipulau stanau netrajalasravaiḥ cintayantī na śokasya tadāntam adhigacchati
english: She, bathing her ample breasts with the flow of tears from her eyes, could find no end to her grief even as she reflected.

sanskrit: sā vepamānā patitā pravāte kadalī yathā rākṣasīnāṃ bhayatrastā vivarṇavadanābhavat
english: Trembling like a plantain tree fallen in a gust of wind, stricken with fear of the rākṣasīs, she became pale of face.

sanskrit: tasyā sā dīrghavipulā vepantyāḥ sītayā tadā dadṛśe kampinī veṇī vyālīva parisarpatī
english: Then the long, thick braid of trembling Sītā was seen quivering like a serpent crawling along.

sanskrit: sā niḥśvasantī duḥkhārtā śokopahatacetanā ārtā vyasṛjad aśrūṇi maithilī vilalāpa ha
english: She, sighing deeply, afflicted by suffering, her senses struck down by grief, distressed, shed tears — Maithilī lamented.

sanskrit: hā rāmeti ca duḥkhārtā punar hā lakṣmaṇeti ca hā śvaśru mama kausalye hā sumitreti bhāvini
english: "Ah, Rāma!" she cried, afflicted by pain, then again "Ah, Lakṣmaṇa! Ah, my mother-in-law Kausalyā! Ah, Sumitrā, dear to me!"

sanskrit: lokapravādaḥ satyo 'yaṃ paṇḍitaiḥ samudāhṛtaḥ akāle durlabho mṛtyuḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā
english: "This saying repeated by the wise is indeed true: death is hard to come by at the wrong time, whether for a woman or a man."

sanskrit: yatrāham ābhiḥ krūrābhī rākṣasībhir ihārditā jīvāmi hīnā rāmeṇa muhūrtam api duḥkhitā
english: "For here I am, tormented by these cruel rākṣasīs in this place, living — bereft of Rāma, suffering — even for a single moment."

sanskrit: eṣālpapuṇyā kṛpaṇā vinaśiṣyāmy anāthavat samudramadhye nau pūrṇā vāyuvegair ivāhatā
english: "I, this one of little merit, wretched, shall perish without a protector, like a fully laden boat struck by the force of wind in the middle of the ocean."

sanskrit: bhartāraṃ tam apaśyantī rākṣasīvaśam āgatā sīdāmi khalu śokena kūlaṃ toyahataṃ yathā
english: "Not seeing that husband of mine, having fallen under the power of rākṣasīs, I sink in grief like a river-bank undermined by water."

sanskrit: taṃ padmadalapatrākṣaṃ siṃhavikrāntagāminam dhanyāḥ paśyanti me nāthaṃ kṛtajñaṃ priyavādinam
english: "Blessed are those who see my lord — he of lotus-petal eyes, lion-like gait, grateful, and dear of speech."

sanskrit: sarvathā tena hīnāyā rāmeṇa viditātmanā tīṣkṇaṃ viṣam ivāsvādya durlabhaṃ mama jīvitam
english: "Bereft in every way of that Rāma of high-souled wisdom, my life is as hard to sustain as though I had swallowed sharp poison."

sanskrit: kīdṛśaṃ tu mayā pāpaṃ purā dehāntare kṛtam yenedaṃ prāpyate duḥkhaṃ mayā ghoraṃ sudāruṇam
english: "What sin did I commit in a previous birth, in another body, on account of which I incur this terrible and most dreadful suffering?"

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ tyaktum icchāmi śokena mahatā vṛtā rākṣasībhiś ca rakṣantyā rāmo nāsādyate mayā
english: "Enveloped in great grief, I wish to abandon my life — guarded as I am by rākṣasīs, Rāma cannot be reached by me."

sanskrit: dhig astu khalu mānuṣyaṃ dhig astu paravaśyatām na śakyaṃ yat parityaktum ātmacchandena jīvitam
english: "Shame indeed upon being mortal, shame upon being under another's power — that one cannot abandon life of one's own free will."

sanskrit: prasaktāśrumukhīty evaṃ bruvantī janakātmajā adhomukhamukhī bālā vilaptum upacakrame
english: Speaking thus, with her face streaming with tears, the young daughter of Janaka, her face cast downward, began to lament.

sanskrit: unmatteva pramatteva bhrāntacitteva śocatī upāvṛttā kiśorīva viveṣṭantī mahītale
english: Grieving, like one maddened, like one bewildered, like one whose mind has wandered, she turned about and rolled upon the ground like a young mare.

sanskrit: rāghavasyāpramattasya rakṣasā kāmarūpiṇā rāvaṇena pramathyāham ānītā krośatī balāt
english: "I, belonging to the ever-vigilant Rāghava, have been seized and forcibly brought by the rākṣasa Rāvaṇa, who changes his form at will, though I cried out."

sanskrit: rākṣasī vaśam āpannā bhartyamānā sudāruṇam cintayantī suduḥkhārtā nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: "Having fallen under the power of the rākṣasīs, menaced in a most dreadful manner, reflecting on all this and afflicted by the deepest sorrow, I dare not live."

sanskrit: na hi me jīvitenārtho naivārthair na ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ vasantyā rākṣasī madhye vinā rāmaṃ mahāratham
english: "I have no use for life, nor for riches, nor for ornaments, dwelling in the midst of rākṣasīs without Rāma, the great warrior."

sanskrit: dhiṅ mām anāryām asatīṃ yāhaṃ tena vinā kṛtā muhūrtam api rakṣāmi jīvitaṃ pāpajīvitā
english: "Shame on me, ignoble and wicked — who preserves her life even for a moment, having been separated from him; living this sinful life."

sanskrit: kā ca me jīvite śraddhā sukhe vā taṃ priyaṃ vinā bhartāraṃ sāgarāntāyā vasudhāyāḥ priyaṃ vadam
english: "What faith do I have in life or in happiness, without that dear husband of mine, beloved of all the earth bounded by the ocean?"

sanskrit: bhidyatāṃ bhakṣyatāṃ vāpi śarīraṃ visṛjāmy aham na cāpy ahaṃ ciraṃ duḥkhaṃ saheyaṃ priyavarjitā
english: "Let my body be torn apart or devoured — I am giving it up. For I could not long endure this suffering bereft of my beloved."

sanskrit: caraṇenāpi savyena na spṛśeyaṃ niśācaram rāvaṇaṃ kiṃ punar ahaṃ kāmayeyaṃ vigarhitam
english: "I would not touch the night-wanderer Rāvaṇa even with my left foot — how then could I desire that contemptible one?"

sanskrit: pratyākhyātaṃ na jānāti nātmānaṃ nātmanaḥ kulam yo nṛśaṃsa svabhāvena māṃ prārthayitum icchati
english: "He who is cruel by nature and desires to court me does not know he has been rejected, nor does he know himself or his own lineage."

sanskrit: chinnā bhinnā vibhaktā vā dīpte vāgnau pradīpitā rāvaṇaṃ nopatiṣṭheyaṃ kiṃ pralāpena vaś ciram
english: "Cut to pieces, torn asunder, divided, or cast into blazing fire — I would still not submit to Rāvaṇa. What is the use of this babble to you at length?"

sanskrit: khyātaḥ prājñaḥ kṛtajñaś ca sānukrośaś ca rāghavaḥ sadvṛtto niranukrośaḥ śaṅke madbhāgyasaṃkṣayāt
english: "Rāghava is renowned as wise, grateful, and compassionate, virtuous in conduct. I suspect it is from the exhaustion of my own fortune that he shows no compassion."

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ janasthāne sahasrāṇi caturdaśa yenaikena nirastāni sa māṃ kiṃ nābhipadyate
english: "He who alone drove away fourteen thousand rākṣasas at Janasthāna — why does that one not come to me?"

sanskrit: niruddhā rāvaṇenāham alpavīryeṇa rakṣasā samarthaḥ khalu me bhartā rāvaṇaṃ hantum āhave
english: "I am confined by Rāvaṇa, a rākṣasa of little true valor. My husband is indeed capable of slaying Rāvaṇa in battle."

sanskrit: virādho daṇḍakāraṇye yena rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ raṇe rāmeṇa nihataḥ sa māṃ kiṃ nābhipadyate
english: "He by whom Virādha, that bull among rākṣasas, was slain in battle in the Daṇḍaka forest — why does that Rāma not come to me?"

sanskrit: kāmaṃ madhye samudrasya laṅkeyaṃ duṣpradharṣaṇā na tu rāghavabāṇānāṃ gatirodhī ha vidyate
english: "Indeed this Laṅkā in the midst of the ocean may be difficult to assail, yet there exists no obstacle to the passage of Rāghava's arrows."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tat kāraṇaṃ yena rāmo dṛḍhaparākramaḥ rakṣasāpahṛtāṃ bhāryām iṣṭāṃ nābhyavapadyate
english: "What then is the reason why Rāma, of firm valor, does not come for his beloved wife who has been abducted by a rākṣasa?"

sanskrit: ihasthāṃ māṃ na jānīte śaṅke lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ jānann api hi tejasvī dharṣaṇāṃ marṣayiṣyati
english: "I suspect that Lakṣmaṇa's elder brother does not know I am here. For knowing it, that fiery hero would not tolerate this violation."

sanskrit: hṛteti yo 'dhigatvā māṃ rāghavāya nivedayet gṛdhrarājo 'pi sa raṇe rāvaṇena nipātitaḥ
english: "Even the king of the vultures, Jaṭāyu, who found me and would have reported to Rāghava that I had been taken away, has been struck down in battle by Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ karma mahat tena māṃ tadābhyavapadyatā tiṣṭhatā rāvaṇadvandve vṛddhenāpi jaṭāyuṣā
english: "A great deed was done by old Jaṭāyu, who at that time came to my aid and stood in single combat against Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: yadi mām iha jānīyād vartamānāṃ sa rāghavaḥ adya bāṇair abhikruddhaḥ kuryāl lokam arākṣasaṃ
english: "If that Rāghava knew I am here in this state, he would today, with his arrows, enraged, rid the world of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: vidhamec ca purīṃ laṅkāṃ śoṣayec ca mahodadhim rāvaṇasya ca nīcasya kīrtiṃ nāma ca nāśayet
english: "He would scatter the city of Laṅkā and dry up the great ocean, and he would destroy the name and fame of the vile Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: tato nihatanathānāṃ rākṣasīnāṃ gṛhe gṛhe yathāham evaṃ rudatī tathā bhūyo na saṃśayaḥ anviṣya rakṣasāṃ laṅkāṃ kuryād rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "Then, searching out the Laṅkā of the rākṣasas, Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa would without doubt cause rākṣasī women in every house, their lords slain, to weep just as I weep now."

sanskrit: na hi tābhyāṃ ripur dṛṣṭo muhūtam api jīvati citā dhūmākulapathā gṛdhramaṇḍalasaṃkulā acireṇa tu laṅkeyaṃ śmaśānasadṛśī bhavet
english: "For no enemy seen by those two survives even for an instant. Before long, this Laṅkā would become like a cremation ground, its pathways dense with funeral-pyre smoke and circles of vultures."

sanskrit: acireṇaiva kālena prāpsyāmy eva manoratham duṣprasthāno 'yam ākhyāti sarveṣāṃ vo viparyayaḥ
english: "Before long I shall attain my heart's desire. These omens of evil portent foretell the reversal of fortune for all of you."

sanskrit: yādṛśāni tu dṛśyante laṅkāyām aśubhani tu acireṇaiva kālena bhaviṣyati hataprabhā
english: "As for the inauspicious signs that are visible in Laṅkā — before long she will be robbed of her splendor."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ laṅkā hate pāpe rāvaṇe rākṣasādhipe śoṣaṃ yāsyati durdharṣā pramadā vidhavā yathā
english: "Surely, when the sinful Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, is slain, Laṅkā, formerly invincible, will wither like a widow woman."

sanskrit: puṣyotsavasamṛddhā ca naṣṭabhartrī sarākṣasā bhaviṣyati purī laṅkā naṣṭabhartrī yathāṅganā
english: "The city of Laṅkā, once prosperous with festivities and celebrations, rākṣasas and all, will become a city whose lord is lost, like a woman whose husband has perished."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ rākṣasakanyānāṃ rudantīnāṃ gṛhe gṛhe śroṣyāmi nacirād eva duḥkhārtānām iha dhvanim
english: "Surely before long I shall hear here the sounds of rākṣasa daughters weeping in grief in every house."

sanskrit: sāndhakārā hatadyotā hatarākṣasapuṃgavā bhaviṣyati purī laṅkā nirdagdhā rāmasāyakaiḥ
english: "The city of Laṅkā will be plunged in darkness, stripped of its radiance, its great rākṣasa warriors slain, consumed by Rāma's arrows."

sanskrit: yadi nāma sa śūro māṃ rāmo raktāntalocanaḥ jānīyād vartamānāṃ hi rāvaṇasya niveśane
english: "If only that hero Rāma of red-cornered eyes would come to know that I am dwelling here in Rāvaṇa's abode."

sanskrit: anena tu nṛśaṃsena rāvaṇenādhamena me samayo yas tu nirdiṣṭas tasya kālo 'yam āgataḥ
english: "But the term that was set for me by this cruel and base Rāvaṇa — that time has now arrived."

sanskrit: akāryaṃ ye na jānanti nairṛtāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ adharmāt tu mahotpāto bhaviṣyati hi sāmpratam
english: "These Nairṛtas, doers of evil, who do not know what should not be done — from their unrighteousness a great catastrophe will soon befall."

sanskrit: naite dharmaṃ vijānanti rākṣasāḥ piśitāśanāḥ dhruvaṃ māṃ prātarāśārthe rākṣasaḥ kalpayiṣyati
english: "These rākṣasas, flesh-eaters, do not know what is right. Surely the rākṣasa will prepare me as his morning meal."

sanskrit: sāhaṃ kathaṃ kariṣyāmi taṃ vinā priyadarśanam rāmaṃ raktāntanayanam apaśyantī suduḥkhitā
english: "How shall I, utterly grief-stricken, carry on without him — without seeing that Rāma, lovely to behold, with red-cornered eyes?"

sanskrit: yadi kaś cit pradātā me viṣasyādya bhaved iha kṣipraṃ vaivasvataṃ devaṃ paśyeyaṃ patinā vinā
english: "If there were someone here today who could give me poison, I would quickly behold the god Vaivasvata, separated as I am from my husband."

sanskrit: nājānāj jīvatīṃ rāmaḥ sa māṃ lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ jānantau tau na kuryātāṃ norvyāṃ hi mama mārgaṇam
english: "That Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa's elder brother, does not know I am alive; for if those two knew, they would not fail to search for me across all the earth."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ mamaiva śokena sa vīro lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ devalokam ito yātas tyaktvā dehaṃ mahītale
english: "Surely that hero, the elder of Lakṣmaṇa, has departed from here to the world of the gods, abandoning his body on the earth, out of grief for me alone."

sanskrit: dhanyā devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ mama paśyanti ye nāthaṃ rāmaṃ rājīvalocanam
english: "Blessed are the gods together with the gandharvas, the siddhas and the great seers, who behold my lord Rāma of lotus eyes."

sanskrit: atha vā na hi tasyārthe dharmakāmasya dhīmataḥ mayā rāmasya rājarṣer bhāryayā paramātmanaḥ
english: "Or perhaps for the sake of that wise Rāma, devoted to dharma, that royal sage of the highest spirit — for his sake, as his wife —"

sanskrit: dṛśyamāne bhavet prītaḥ sauhṛdaṃ nāsty apaśyataḥ nāśayanti kṛtaghrās tu na rāmo nāśayiṣyati
english: "— when seen, he would rejoice; when unseen, there is no friendship. Ingrates destroy, but Rāma will not destroy."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu me na guṇāḥ ke cit kiṃ vā bhāgya kṣayo hi me yāhaṃ sītā varārheṇa hīnā rāmeṇa bhāminī
english: "Do I then have no virtues whatsoever, or is it the exhaustion of my fortune, that I, Sītā, am separated from Rāma who deserves the best, I who am so passionate?"

sanskrit: śreyo me jīvitān martuṃ vihīnā yā mahātmanā rāmād akliṣṭacāritrāc chūrāc chatrunibarhaṇāt
english: "Better for me to die than to live, bereft as I am of that great-souled Rāma of unblemished conduct, that hero who destroys enemies."

sanskrit: atha vā nyastaśastrau tau vane mūlaphalāśanau bhrātarau hi nara śreṣṭhau carantau vanagocarau
english: "Or perhaps those two best of men, the brothers, have laid down their weapons and roam the forest living on roots and fruits, wandering through the wilderness."

sanskrit: atha vā rākṣasendreṇa rāvaṇena durātmanā chadmanā ghātitau śūrau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "Or perhaps those two heroes, the brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, have been slain by deception by the evil-souled lord of rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: sāham evaṃgate kāle martum icchāmi sarvathā na ca me vihito mṛtyur asmin duḥkhe 'pi vartati
english: "I, with matters having come to this pass, wish in every way to die — yet death is not ordained for me even as I endure this suffering."

sanskrit: dhanyāḥ khalu mahātmāno munayaḥ satyasaṃmatāḥ jitātmāno mahābhāgā yeṣāṃ na staḥ priyāpriye
english: "Truly blessed are those great-souled sages who are honored as truthful, who have conquered the self, the greatly fortunate ones, for whom pleasant and unpleasant do not exist."

sanskrit: priyān na saṃbhaved duḥkham apriyād adhikaṃ bhayam tābhyāṃ hi ye viyujyante namas teṣāṃ mahātmanām
english: "From what is dear, grief does not arise; from what is unpleasant arises fear — greater than grief. Homage to those great souls who are free from both."

sanskrit: sāhaṃ tyaktā priyeṇeha rāmeṇa viditātmanā prāṇāṃs tyakṣyāmi pāpasya rāvaṇasya gatā vaśam
english: "I, abandoned here by my dear Rāma of high wisdom, having fallen under the power of the sinful Rāvaṇa, shall give up my life."
